biography: Cooper MacNeil, a 25-year-old American with a steely gaze and a mop of black curls, isn't your typical silver-spoon racer. While motorsport pedigree might have opened doors, his relentless determination slammed them wide open. Growing up near Road Atlanta, the roar of engines was Cooper's lullaby. He badgered his father for karting lessons, showcasing a natural aptitude that belied his age. His first taste of competitive racing came at 14, a local karting series where his raw talent quickly turned heads. A defining moment came at Sebring in 2020. During a torrential downpour, several seasoned drivers spun off, but Cooper, in his Porsche 911 RSR GTE, navigated the treacherous conditions with remarkable composure, ultimately securing a podium finish. This performance solidified his reputation as a rising star, capable of handling immense pressure. Now, as a rising talent, Cooper continues to refine his skills, aiming for the top step in every race and demonstrating a maturity beyond his years. He's a force to be reckoned with, a blend of raw talent and unwavering dedication.
drivingStyle: Cooper's driving style is characterized by a blend of calculated aggression and remarkable consistency. He's not one for flamboyant, last-minute overtakes. Instead, he prefers to build momentum throughout a race, meticulously managing tire wear and fuel consumption. He attacks corners with precision, prioritizing exit speed over dramatic entries. Under pressure, Cooper remains remarkably calm, rarely making rash decisions. His ability to maintain focus and deliver consistent lap times, even in the face of adversity, is his greatest strength. He is known to be a team player, always willing to listen to his engineers and adapt his driving to the needs of the car.

careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the GTE Am class after a grueling battle, proving his ability to perform under the most demanding circumstances and cementing his legacy as a top endurance racer.
